structuralViolations.clause: §A2.3, table row 1: "**§2 K20** — `emittable(kind) = ownerClassKeys(kind) ∩ capabilityRegistry ≠ ∅`" (line 5939); same identifier again in §A1.1 P-09: "so `ownerClassKeys(CONSENT_STATE) ∩ capabilityRegistry = ∅` and K20 derives `emittable = false`" (line 5838).
structuralViolations.consequence: `capabilityRegistry` is declared by NO shape anywhere in the contract — grep confirms exactly two occurrences, both these, and zero declarations. This is the identifier round 3 removed from K20 for precisely that reason, and the repair was applied at the declaration site only. Two consequences follow. (1) §0.1 F2 is violated on its own terms: its mechanism is "a build test resolves every identifier cited in a normative sentence against a declaration," and Annex A is declared normative at §A0.1 — that test fails on Annex A. (2) The restatement contradicts the rule it cites. §2.4 K20 now reads `∃ k ∈ ownerClassKeys(kind) : k ∈ REGISTERED_KEYS` and says the key set is space-qualified "and **never** a bare name"; §A2.3 states the same derivation using a bare name. §2 K20 does not say what §A2.3 claims it says. The divergence is currently harmless in value — `ownerClassKeys` returns C9-space refs today and F24 proves AE ∩ C9 = ∅ — but the space qualification is exactly what stops a TOOL-space owner-class ref from matching a C9 spelling (F24: all 47 catalogue names ARE C9-CAP keys), and K20 is the derivation that decides whether a kind may be emitted at all. §A0.2 classifies this itself: "A divergence between this annex and the body is a defect in one of them, to be repaired, not adjudicated."
structuralViolations.fix: In §A2.3's first table row replace the formula with K20's current text — `emittable(kind) = ∃ k ∈ ownerClassKeys(kind) : k ∈ REGISTERED_KEYS` — and in §A1.1 P-09's status cell replace `∩ capabilityRegistry = ∅` with `∩ REGISTERED_KEYS = ∅`. Two one-line edits; no rule changes.

structuralViolations.clause: §A1.6.2 (line 5898, marked "**A1.6.2 — NORMATIVE**"): "§0.7 F32 defines `CONSENT(cap) := cap.targetKind ∈ {client_consent, client_consent_security}`, which this key satisfies".
structuralViolations.consequence: F32 does not define `CONSENT(cap)` as that. F32 (lines 488–490) defines it as that disjunct **∨ `cap.actionClass ∈ {record_client_consent, invalidate_client_consent_authority}`**. §A1.6.2 presents one of two disjuncts, with the definitional operator `:=`, as the whole definition of a conferral-fence predicate — inside the one clause §A0.1 names as an original normative rule of the annex. This is the identical defect round 3 repaired in §3.4 ("§3.4's copy carried only the `actionClass` half of a two-disjunct predicate — the way a fence comes to mean two things"), reproduced with the other half and left standing. §3.4 was fixed by pointing at F32 without restating; §A1.6.2 still restates. The narrower predicate is the weaker fence: F32 itself records why the disjunct exists — "a capability registered later under one of those action classes with a different `targetKind` would otherwise escape" — so an implementer taking A1.6.2's definition builds precisely the escape F32's second disjunct closes. Not live today (F32 records both halves resolve to the same three capabilities by execution), and F32 governs under §A0.1, so nothing is currently under-fenced.
structuralViolations.fix: In §A1.6.2 replace the quoted definition with a non-restating reference: "§0.7 F32's `CONSENT(cap)` — whose `targetKind` disjunct this key satisfies". One line; it also brings the annex into line with the no-restatement discipline §3.4 now follows.

structuralViolations.clause: §3.11 R3.11.5 (line 4443): "A capability whose owner queues dispatch after `APPROVED` … declares `dispatch_is_synchronous: false` in the widget capability policy table. For such a capability `mintIntent()` refuses to mint a `REQUEST_APPROVAL` or `COMMIT` intent…" — together with §0.7 F28's gloss on the same column (line 419): "false where the owner queues dispatch after `APPROVED`, so a `REQUEST_APPROVAL` or `COMMIT` naming it refuses until the owner declares it".
structuralViolations.consequence: As written, the lookup can never resolve for any intent the rule governs. §0.12 F69 and §3.2 R3.2.2 permit `REQUEST_APPROVAL` and `COMMIT` to carry an **AE** ref and only an AE ref; §0.7 F28 makes `WIDGET_CAPABILITY_POLICY` "total over C9-CAP's 56 rows, **and over those only**" and states its columns "have no meaning over AE-CAP". So `WIDGET_CAPABILITY_POLICY[capKey(commitRef)]` is `undefined` for every capability R3.11.5 addresses, the flag is never `false`, and the refusal never fires. An implementation cannot satisfy both clauses: giving the table AE rows violates F28, and not giving it AE rows makes R3.11.5 inoperative. The direction matters — this one fails OPEN, not closed: the live case is `communication.bulk-campaign.admit.v2`, the single allowlisted `MARKETING_FANOUT` row, reachable as a `REQUEST_APPROVAL` from `CLIENT_LIST`, and queued-after-`APPROVED` dispatch is exactly what R3.11.5 exists to refuse. The contract already has the correct idiom one section away: §0.14 F80 spells it out as "its **C9 propose key's** `WIDGET_CAPABILITY_POLICY` row", which is total and well-defined because F31 asserts every allowlisted AE key is the `ae` side of exactly one `AE_PROPOSE_PAIRING` row. R3.11.5 and F28 omit that phrase, so the mechanism as specified cannot be built, and its marking is `[TO BUILD]` — which means "not built yet", not "not buildable as written" — rather than `NORMATIVE-PENDING`.
structuralViolations.fix: Adopt F80's wording in both places: R3.11.5 → "…whose **C9 propose key's** `WIDGET_CAPABILITY_POLICY` row declares `dispatch_is_synchronous: false`"; F28's column gloss → "…so a `REQUEST_APPROVAL` or `COMMIT` whose pairing row names it as `propose` refuses until the owner declares it". Two one-line edits; the fence becomes constructible and total without adding a row to any table.

structuralViolations.clause: §2.4 K20 (line 2622): "…and **never** a bare name: an intersection against an unqualified key set would match a C9 key against an AE spelling, which §0.6 F24 shows is a real collision and not a hypothetical one."
structuralViolations.consequence: F24 shows the opposite of that specific pairing. F24 (line 386) states "**AE-CAP ∩ (C9-CAP ∪ TOOL-DEF) = ∅** — the two spaces share no spelling," so a C9 key matching an AE spelling is the one cross-space match F24 proves impossible. The real collision F24 documents is TOOL-DEF ⊂ C9-CAP — all 47 catalogue names are C9-CAP keys — and that is the collision space qualification actually prevents here, since `ownerClassKeys` returns `ReadonlySet<CapabilityRef>` and a TOOL-space ref would match a C9 spelling in a bare-name set. The rule K20 states is correct and conservative either way, and F24's closing sentence ("the only way to see that is to name the space") independently supports it — so the consequence is confined to the stated ground, which a reader who follows the citation finds contradicted. I flag this as the weakest of the four: a charitable reading takes "a C9 key against an AE spelling" as loose shorthand for cross-space matching generally, for which F24 does supply a real instance. It is reported because it was introduced by the round-3 repair and is the class of defect round 3 itself was strict about.
structuralViolations.fix: Name the pair F24 actually proves: "…would match a TOOL-space key against a C9 spelling, which §0.6 F24 shows is a real collision and not a hypothetical one — all 47 catalogue names are C9-CAP keys." One line.

confirm.verdict:
NOT CERTIFIABLE — but narrowly, and I want to be exact about what that word is carrying, because three of the four findings are one-line edits and none of them touches authority.

ZERO security-contract violations. ZERO unproven normative claims. The authority spine is intact and I verified every element of it against the source text rather than against the evidence files.

WHAT HOLDS, each checked directly:
— Exactly TWO floor reductions, both in §0.17 F91's table (the nine non-catalogue C9-CAP keys; the five `FLOOR_EXEMPT` intents). No third reduction anywhere: §3.4 R3.4.8 and §3.16.8 both refuse to re-enumerate and point at §0.17, and R3.4.8 says why ("a contract with two places claiming to list all its reductions has no place that does"). §0.17's `C9_RESOURCE_FLOOR['SOURCE_READ'] = ANONYMOUS` paragraph is the removal of a raise that was never in force, not a third reduction.
— §2.6.7 CLIENT.2 (line 2868) intact: the `validateEnvelope` refusal of a `CLIENT_LIST` at `presentation_mode: 'client'`, "with no exception and no subject test". Unrenumbered — CLIENT.3 sits beside it at 2869 — and unsuperseded. §2.6.22 ARTIFACT.3 (line 3300) intact: `contains_pii` stated before fetch. Unrenumbered — ARTIFACT.5 at 3302 — and unsuperseded.
— Gate 5 (line 4191) recomputes `verificationFloor(record, record.widget_kind)` from an `IntentRecord` and the live tables, compares against its OWN result, and refuses on ANY difference in either direction. The record genuinely satisfies `FloorSubject`: §3.7 carries `effect`, `capability`, `handoff_capability_ref`, `target`, `priority` and `widget_kind`, which is exactly F43's closed input list — so the exempt branch is recomputable too, which was the point of adding `priority`.
— Gate 6 (lines 4203–4244) binds `const ref = subjectCapability(record)` once and dispatches on it, explicitly "NOT record.capability". The `HANDOFF` branch resolves destination fences only — registration in space, `SENSITIVE_DEST`, `targetFloor('s')`, the landing surface's own ingress — and never `assertCanExecute`, never `c9Capability`'s domain/mode admission, never the AE commit allowlist. The null guard is present and correct.
— Gate 7 (line 4193) re-reads `requiredConfirmationKind(subjectCapability(record))` from the LIVE allowlist and refuses a key whose row was withdrawn between mint and submission. Round 2's repair is still standing.
— No precedence chain, Annex A included. §A0.2 states it affirmatively and gives the reason the two subjects cannot overlap; §A0.1 names the annex's only two original rules (§A1.6.2, §A2.8) and both are within its one subject.
— No erratum cited in normative text: I scanned every line before Annex B for E-n / EB-n / EC-n and got zero hits. Annex B is correctly fenced `[NON-NORMATIVE]` and binding on nothing.
— FR-1 … FR-16 over 21 rows, all holding. SIX hold outright: FR-6a (engine fence `[EXISTS]` — `VERIFIED_CLIENT_CHANNEL` + `assertConsentChannelBinding`), FR-6c (the `admit.v2` owner-approval fence, `[EXISTS]` and running today), FR-6e (cross-tenant half `[EXISTS]`), FR-6f (`decideApproval` `[EXISTS]`, bounded by F90(4)'s `controlledFixtureMode` caveat on P-27), FR-8 (boundary half `[EXISTS]`), FR-16 (the property holds; only the test is absent). — Registry cardinalities, by execution, exact: 226 / 221 / 47 / 56.

WHY THE VERDICT IS STILL NO. Four findings, all in the checkers' blind spots, all structural under the criteria as given:
(1) `capabilityRegistry` — an identifier NO shape declares — survives in two normative Annex A clauses (§A2.3, §A1.1 P-09) after round 3 removed it from §2.4 K20. This is the one repair on the named list that was made at the rule and not closed over the clauses reading it, and §A2.3 now states the emittability derivation in the bare-name form K20 says it must "never" take.
(2) §A1.6.2 — itself marked NORMATIVE — states `CONSENT(cap) := cap.targetKind ∈ {…}` and attributes it to §0.7 F32, which defines it with a second `actionClass` disjunct. Same defect class round 3 fixed in §3.4, reproduced with the other half.
(3) §3.11 R3.11.5's `dispatch_is_synchronous` fence reads `WIDGET_CAPABILITY_POLICY` for a capability that F69 requires to be AE-space and F28 says that table cannot hold — so the refusal never fires, and it fails OPEN on the one live case (`communication.bulk-campaign.admit.v2`). §0.14 F80 already has the constructible idiom one section away ("its C9 propose key's row"); R3.11.5 and F28's gloss omit it.
(4) §2.4 K20's justification cites §0.6 F24 for a C9↔AE spelling collision that F24 explicitly proves empty; the real collision F24 documents is TOOL ⊂ C9, which is also the one space-qualification actually guards against here. Weakest of the four, reported with its charitable reading stated.

WHAT I WOULD TELL THE OWNER. This is not a document that needs another round. Findings 1, 2 and 4 are single-line text edits that change no rule and no value; finding 3 is a single-line edit that adopts wording the contract already uses in §0.14 F80. Nothing in the four requires re-deriving anything, re-verifying any cardinality, or re-opening any fence. The correct disposition is: make the four edits, re-run the four checkers (which will stay green — none of these live where they can see), and ship. If the bar were "no defect that changes what any rule means or what any authority can do," this contract meets it today and I would say so plainly. It fails only the literal bar the brief sets, on citation accuracy, in four places, and I am reporting it that way rather than rounding it up or down.

adversarial.round3RepairNotes:
All eight round-3 repairs confirmed in place and, where they were more than hygiene, attacked directly.

1. risk_tier retyping. StrategyOptionsBody.alternatives[].risk_tier (line 2964) and ApprovalBody.risk_tier (line 2993) are both Cell<'read'|'low_write'|'medium_write'|'high_write'|'restricted'>, each annotated "a rendered datum, so a Cell (§1.2 V1)". ConfirmationRequirement.risk_tier (line 3899) is deliberately the bare union, with the reason stated in the shape itself: "NOT a Cell: this is an intent-side member, never a body leaf, so §1.2 V1 does not reach it, and §4.4.3 classifies it AUDIT_RETAINED — a Cell's minted label would be conversation content on an authority-side field." I attacked this asymmetry and it survives: V1 and F63 both scope the leaf taxonomy to `body` explicitly ("The taxonomy governs `body` only"), so V1 genuinely does not reach an intent-side member; and §4.4.3's IntentRecord table (line 4964) does classify `confirmation` (risk tier, reversibility, audience size, requires_readback, readback_ref, consent_scope) AUDIT_RETAINED, so a Cell.label there would put a CONVERSATION_CONTENT-shaped minted string on a field F15's build-time reachability test must admit on the path to Gate 11/13/14. The apparent inconsistency that `reversible` IS a Cell on all three shapes is separately justified and not arbitrary: R3.6.1 and E-24 record that the only canonical upstream value is the literal 'SOURCE_DEFINED', which is not a boolean, so only a Cell can carry it as NOT_MEASURED. Two different fields, two stated reasons, no drift.

2. renderTextEquivalent arity. Declared once at arity 5 in §1.9 H2: `presentation.text_equivalent = renderTextEquivalent(kind, body, cell_index, intents, locale)`. §2.3.5 K9 cites it as "declared in §1.9 H2, at arity five — (kind, body, cell_index, intents, locale) — and is not restated here", and the parameter list matches H2 byte-for-byte. adversarial.verdict:
THE BAR IS MET. I could not find a violation, and after a full adversarial pass I am saying so plainly rather than manufacturing one.

I read all 6,201 lines, ran the four committed checkers (all clean), ran two further probes, and verified every repository-facing number by loading the modules and enumerating them in process. Not one enumeration was off. 226/221/47/56 exact; the nine C9 extras with their exact modes and resource classes; mode 41/13/2 and resourceClass 40/15/1; LOCAL unique to c9.no_action; BOOKING 13/7, CONSENT 3, IDENTITY 6, MARKETING_FANOUT 4, TENANT_AUTHORITY 28/14, MONEY 92 and 39-of-105 against 12/4 for the bare token; ALLOW 129 / SHADOW_ONLY 95 / DENY 2; 105 reachable, 53 excluded by source type; 98 risk facets; the seven autonomy levels at 19/95/1/50/42/14/5; 19 REQUIRED all on 'tenant-owner'; 164 of 221 on the twelve-role default; zero definitions carrying authenticated_request in trustedServiceSourceTypes. Every F38 pairing row resolves on both sides, every F37 gap key names a real capability with the stated disposition, every F36 must-resolve key resolves, and all eleven deleted/reserved names resolve in no space.

THE SEVEN NAMED CHECKS. (1) Exactly two floor reductions, both in §0.17, and §3.4.8 and §3.16.8 both refuse to enumerate them a second time — "a contract with two places claiming to list all its reductions has no place that does." Row 1's arithmetic is exact: I executed the registry and the three SOURCE_HANDOFF extras (b35.preview PROPOSE_ONLY, b35.confirm and a22.configuration OWNER_HANDOFF) all floor at SESSION_VERIFIED through both C9_MODE_FLOOR and C9_RESOURCE_FLOOR, the five SOURCE_READ extras are all mode READ so both terms return ANONYMOUS and the floor reduces to their own policy row plus consent class exactly as stated, and c9.no_action is mode READ and resourceClass LOCAL so ANONYMOUS is correct. (2) CLIENT.2 (§2.6.7, line 2868) is intact at its own number and states its own validateEnvelope refusal directly rather than citing the retired "display fence"; CLIENT.3 is a distinct clause about bulk_intents roles. ARTIFACT.3 (§2.6.22, line 3300) is intact as the contains_pii clause; ARTIFACT.5 is the distinct fixed-roles clause. Neither is renumbered, superseded, or collided with — the mechanical audit counts exactly one of each of the four. (3) Gate 5 calls verificationFloor(record, record.widget_kind), and IntentRecord structurally satisfies FloorSubject: it carries effect, capability, handoff_capability_ref, target, priority and widget_kind, all typed as the derivation reads them, all mint class D, all AUDIT_RETAINED so erasure cannot make the recompute undecidable. F42 and R3.7's inline comments state the exact reason priority is there. Recomputable, including the exempt branch. (4) Gate 6 in full binds `const ref = subjectCapability(record)` once and dispatches on it, never on record.capability — and the HANDOFF branch sits above the space dispatch and resolves destination fences only: registration in its space, SENSITIVE_DEST, targetFloor('s') at Gate 5, the landing surface's own ingress, and explicitly never assertCanExecute, never c9Capability's domain/mode admission, never the AE commit allowlist. The reason is given and is correct: applying an execute-admission test to a destination would stop a BUSINESS_INTELLIGENCE run from even offering the a22.configuration or b35.confirm handoff. (5) Gate 7 re-reads requiredConfirmationKind(subjectCapability(record)) from the live allowlist and refuses a key whose row was withdrawn between mint and submission — named in the gate row as F72's second evaluation point. subjectCapability is non-null for a COMMIT by the effect table, so the non-nullable signature is satisfied. (6) No precedence chain anywhere, Annex A included: A0.2 states there is none and explains why none is needed, and rules that a divergence is "a defect in one of them, to be repaired, not adjudicated." The checker finds no precedence language and no erratum citation in normative text. (7) The FR table is 21 rows over 16 rules and every row holds. Fifteen hold only fail-closed and I have listed them; the ones that hold on a running fence are FR-6a (engine-side actorPolicy VERIFIED_CLIENT_CHANNEL plus assertConsentChannelBinding), FR-6c (admit.v2's owner-only approval-bound AE fence, which I confirmed is registered REQUIRED and ALLOW), FR-6e (cross-tenant assertion), FR-6f (decideApproval's approver-policy roles, which I read in the kernel), and FR-16 (the property holds by construction — the contract adds no field to either registry, which I confirmed). FR-8 is genuinely mixed: the widget-side shape is absent but the Action Engine provider boundary exists and runs. Every status column is honest; not one of them overstates.

WHERE I ATTACKED HARDEST AND FOUND NOTHING. The authority spine end to end: a channel cannot confer (profiles are monotone-reductive by a property test, max_verification_level is a ceiling only, profile_id is advisory and E15 plus R3.8.3 assert no gate keys its antecedent on it — I checked Gate 8-R specifically, which keys on record.confirmation.requires_readback, server-set and sealed inside body_hash, and which also refuses a readback_ack on a record that does not require one, closing the obvious skip). A kind cannot confer (presentation_mode is derived with no composer field and a byte-identical-intent-set property test; Gate 7 re-derives the kind rule over the widget layer's own record). A button cannot confer (authority_hint is read by nothing, Gate 14's answer governs any Gate 6 disagreement and a disagreement is refused rather than resolved in Gate 6's favour). A role cannot confer (Gate 6 reads Membership/Staff/Client binding and never presentation_mode, profile_id or a11y_env). I tried to build a conferral through the FLOOR_EXEMPT waiver, which is the only place a floor is given up: a priority-0 class-s HANDOFF to a non-sensitive AE destination does escape aeFloor's allowlist requirement — but a HANDOFF never invokes its destination (R3.5.3 names its four readers and no invoker; Gate 13 routes it to a signed target with no capability invoker), SENSITIVE_DEST fails closed on an unregistered or unclassified destination, R3.5.4 refuses a handoff whose surface has not shipped, and the landing surface authenticates at its own ingress. §0.17 row 2 discloses exactly this residual and gives exactly this reason. That is a disclosed reduction, not a conferral. I also confirmed the three build vetoes make an actuating exempt intent unconstructible, and that priority is server-set so an author cannot promote into the set.

I attacked all twenty-one "declared in §X and not restated here" sentences individually, including the ones the committed audit's 25-line lookahead cannot reach. The riskiest is §3.4's, which names subjectCapability among artefacts with "one declaration in this contract, in §0.8" while §3.5 — the next subsection, inside §3 — carries its body. This is the exception F6a names explicitly and admits ("a declare signature in the section whose derivation depends on it, paired with exactly one body in the owning section (subjectCapability is the only instance)"), it is the only instance, both §0.8 F41 and §3.5 say so in terms, and there is no third statement of either. Not a violation.

THREE OBSERVATIONS THAT DO NOT MEET THE BAR, reported so the record is complete and so a "clean" verdict is not mistaken for a shallow one. First, §3's preamble (line 3343) says §3 "is the sole definition of ... the verification-floor derivation ... and the fundamental rules" — two artefacts that §0.2 F6's map assigns to §0 and that §3.4 and §3.14 themselves hand back ("declared in §0.8 and is not restated here"; "declared in §0.16 F89 and are not restated here"). It is a stale scope blurb left over from before the consolidation moved both. It declares nothing, imposes nothing an implementation can violate, and its only failure mode — a future editor restoring a copy in §3 — is exactly what F6a's one-declaration test catches, which the mechanical audit already runs green (verificationFloor: 1, FR table: 1). A one-line fix if the owner wants it; not a rule conflict. Second, §0.8 F41's inline comment says the body lives in "§3.5, which §0.2's map gives the subject capability and the consent fence" — §0.2's map names subjectCapability under §0's Owns column and names neither item for §3. It is a wrong sentence inside a `//` comment, and this contract's own discipline (§1.0, R3.7.2, EC-23, and the mechanical audit's check that no amendment hides in a comment) is that a comment is not a rule. Third, F72's measurement "routes 118 of 226 capabilities — 94 of the 105 widget-reachable — onto SETTINGS_DRAFT" is loosely scoped in its first half: I executed the two-test chain and it routes 202 of 226, while 118 is the count over the 129 ALLOW rows; the second half, 94 of 105, is exact. The number is rationale for why a derivation with a default branch is not a fence, and the true figure is worse than the stated one, so the conclusion is strengthened rather than weakened and F72's operative content — a lookup with no default branch — is unaffected.

None of the three is a structural violation, a security-contract violation, or an unproven normative claim as the owner defined those terms. No two normative clauses cannot both be satisfied; no normative clause names an identifier no shape declares; every function declared total is total (subjectFloor dispatches over four spaces by type with a named fail-closed default per branch, c9Floor and aeFloor call only the pure non-throwing ReadonlyMap lookups F23 declares, SENSITIVE_DEST is total over four spaces and fails closed three ways, nameSourceOf is total by type over the closed seven-member union with `el` bound inside every branch, suffixFor and resolveInteractive and refKey and capKey are each total and injective where they claim to be); every closed set is closed (22 kinds, 8 effect classes, 11 evaluation points, 3 control keys, 5 target classes, 7 InteractiveRef members, 12 RoleHint members, 5 DraftClass members, 5 CellState branches); no assertion set can never pass (F31's start-up set is satisfiable by F34's declared membership, which I checked row by row against the live registry, including that all four members carry autonomyLevel L2_CONFIRMED_REQUEST so the booking commit path floors at SESSION_VERIFIED and is not accidentally dead); no rule has two canonical declarations; and no citation I could find in normative text misstates its target.

This artefact is certifiable. The mechanisms are not running — the widget layer does not exist in any form, and Annex A says so without flinching — but that is declared, bound to prerequisite rows, and fail-closed while pending, which is a checkable property rather than an unproven claim. Ship it.
